also: if it’s necessary for your health

evidence: Cic. Fam. 14.20.1: cētera quae sunt ad vīctum et ad valētūdinem necessāria
terms.comment: As a noun, necessārius is a relative or a close friend, someone bound to one by ties (Lewis & Short).

terms.gloss: it is necessary, one has to
terms.grammar: phrase: with an infinitive, an accusative and infinitive, or a subjunctive
evidence: Publil. Q 75: quidquid plūs quam necesse est possideās, premit
Traupman 56: necesse est tibi manēre in lectō

terms.gloss: there is need, it is needed
terms.grammar: phrase: what is needed in the ablative or as the subject
evidence: Quint. 6.3.66: nōn pluit, nōn opus est tibi
Sen. Ep. 80.4: quid tibi opus est ut sīs bonus?
Cic. Fam. 16.4.2: quod ad valētūdinem opus sit (Lewis & Short s.v. opus)
terms.comment: Not necessary: nihil opus est (see require).

terms.grammar: neuter adjective, only in the nominative and accusative singular, with esse or habēre
evidence: Cic. Fat. 17: nihil fit, quod necesse nōn fuerit (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Sen. 30: nihil necesse est mihi dē mē ipsō dīcere (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The word of necesse est above; an older form is necessum (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: lābrum sī in balineō nōn est, ut sit, item cētera quae sunt ad vīctum et ad valētūdinem necessāria
phrases.english: if there is no basin in the bath, see that there is one, and everything else necessary for food and health

phrases.latin: sīve Aquilō rādit terrās seu brūma nivālem interiōre diem gȳrō trahit, īre necesse est
phrases.english: whether the north wind is scouring the land or midwinter is dragging the snowy day round its shorter circle, I have to go

phrases.latin: nōn pluit, nōn opus est tibi; sī pluit, ipse ūtar
phrases.english: if it isn’t raining, you don’t need it; if it is, I’ll wear it myself

phrases.latin: nec ultrā voluī legere nec opus erat
phrases.english: I didn’t want to read any further, and there was no need
If it is necessary for your health …
If it is necessary for you to stay on …

phrases.latin: sī opus est ad tuam valētūdinem
phrases.english: if it is necessary for your health

debeo.html: Of what has to be, Latin says necesse est; dēbeō with an infinitive is for duty or obligation.

sources: Lewis & Short: necessarius · Lewis & Short: necesse · Lewis & Short: opus
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 56, 350.
